en: The Question on the Characteristic of Feeling (Vedanālakkhaṇapañha)
“Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of feeling?
“It has the characteristic of being felt, Great King, and it has the characteristic of experiencing.
“Suppose, great king, some man were to perform a service for a king, and the king, being pleased, were to grant him an office;
he, endowed and possessed of that office, would enjoy himself provided with the five cords of sensual pleasure.
It might occur to him: ‘Formerly I performed a service for the king, and the king, being pleased with me, granted me an office.’”
‘I gave [this gift], and because of that, I am now experiencing such a feeling.

Or again, Great King, suppose some man, having performed a wholesome deed, after the breakup of the body, after death, were to reappear in a happy destination, in a heavenly world; and there he would [enjoy] the fivefold divine sense-pleasures.
“Suppose he were provided with it and made use of it; then it would occur to him: ‘Indeed, I previously performed wholesome karma;
on that account, I now experience such a feeling.
In this way, Great King, feeling has the characteristic of being felt and the characteristic of experiencing.”
Thus ends the ninth question, on the characteristic of feeling.
